q: Elton John became chairman of Watford in which year?
hint: The club were still a Fourth Division side at the time. It was the year before Graham Taylor arrived as manager.

q: Watford reached their first FA Cup final in 1984, losing at Wembley to which club?
hint: Howard Kendall's side ended a 14-year wait for a trophy that afternoon, and went on to win the league title the following season.

q: Graham Taylor was managing which club when Watford appointed him in 1977?
hint: He had become the Football League's youngest manager there in 1972 and won a divisional title with them in 1976. Grimsby was where he played, not where he managed.

q: The winning side's second goal in the 1984 FA Cup final was hotly disputed, the scorer appearing to head the ball out of Steve Sherwood's hands. Who scored it?
hint: A Scotland centre-forward who had joined the winners earlier that season. His strike partner had already opened the scoring before half-time.

q: Watford finished runners-up in the First Division in 1982-83. Which club took the title ahead of them?
hint: The champions that season were managed by Bob Paisley, in what proved to be his final campaign in charge.

q: By what score did Watford lose the 1984 FA Cup final?
hint: Graeme Sharp scored before half-time and the contested second followed just after it. Watford never replied.

q: Watford signed the young Scottish striker Mo Johnston in November 1983 from which club?
hint: Graham Taylor went north for a forward who had scored 41 goals in 85 games in Scotland. Johnston then hit 20 league goals in 29 games in his first season at Vicarage Road.

q: Watford's 1983-84 UEFA Cup run ended in the third round, beaten 7-2 on aggregate by which club?
hint: The Czechoslovak side won 3-2 at Vicarage Road and then 4-0 at home in December 1983. Watford had already beaten Kaiserslautern and Levski Spartak to get there.

q: Graham Taylor's first season at Watford, 1977-78, ended with the club winning which division?
hint: They were in the bottom tier of the Football League when he arrived, and finished eleven points clear of Southend United.

q: Watford have played their home matches at Vicarage Road since which year?
hint: They moved there from Cassio Road, where they had spent 24 years. The other date on this list is the year the club itself was formed by a merger.

q: Watford reached the 1984 FA Cup final by winning a semi-final at Villa Park against which club?
hint: Their opponents were a Third Division side, and it remains the only time that club has reached an FA Cup semi-final.

q: Which Watford player was sent off at Luton Town in April 1984 and suspended, ruling him out of the FA Cup final?
hint: The left-back was dismissed by referee Roger Milford after a tangle with Luton's Paul Elliott. Les Taylor captained the side at Wembley in his absence.

q: John Barnes left Watford in 1987 to join which club?
hint: The £900,000 move took him to Anfield, where he won two league titles. He had cost Watford next to nothing from non-league Sudbury Court six years earlier.

q: Graham Taylor left Watford in May 1987 to manage which club?
hint: He took his new club straight back to the top flight in 1987-88, then to First Division runners-up in 1989-90, before becoming England manager in 1990.

q: In October 1978, Third Division Watford won a League Cup third-round tie away from home with two Luther Blissett headers. Which club did they knock out?
hint: Watford trailed at half-time at Old Trafford before Blissett's two second-half goals turned it around. It was their first ever win over that opponent.

q: Luther Blissett was sold in 1983, after topping the First Division scoring charts, to which Italian club?
hint: The £1 million move followed his 27-goal league season. He managed only five league goals in Italy and was back at Vicarage Road a year later.

q: Mo Johnston left Watford in October 1984 to join which club?
hint: He returned to Glasgow for around £400,000 and won the Scottish Cup in 1985 and the league in 1986. His notorious move to that club's city rivals came five years later.

q: Watford were relegated from the First Division, ending the top-flight run that began with promotion in 1982, in which season?
hint: It was the season straight after Graham Taylor left. Dave Bassett was sacked in January and Steve Harrison could not save them.

q: Who scored the only goal of Watford's 1984 FA Cup semi-final win?
hint: The 6ft 4in centre-forward headed in a John Barnes cross after eleven minutes. Blissett was in Italy for the whole of that season.

q: Watford, the club that plays at Vicarage Road, are known by which nickname?
hint: The name was adopted alongside the switch to gold and black. Think of the insect those colours belong to.

q: Which club did Watford beat 2-0 in the 1999 First Division play-off final at Wembley?
hint: The beaten finalists came through their semi-final on away goals and played their home games at the Reebok Stadium.

q: Watford reached the 1999 play-off final by beating Birmingham City on penalties in the semi-final. What was the shootout score?
hint: The tie finished 1-1 on aggregate after extra time and the shootout ran deep into sudden death.

q: Who scored Watford's opening goal in the 1999 play-off final, an overhead kick just before half-time?
hint: A different forward added the second goal in the closing minute, so it was not the man who sealed it.

q: Who managed Watford in the 1999 play-off final and through the Premier League season that followed?
hint: He had managed England before returning to the club he first took up the divisions in the 1980s.

q: Who scored the only goal as Watford won 1-0 away at Anfield in August 1999?
hint: He struck inside the opening quarter of an hour at Anfield, past goalkeeper Sander Westerveld.

q: How many points did Watford finish with in the 1999-2000 Premier League season?
hint: They won six of their 38 matches and finished bottom of the table.

q: In which year did Aidy Boothroyd lead Watford to promotion to the Premier League?
hint: They went up via the play-offs, beating Leeds United 3-0 in the final.

q: Ben Foster spent two loan seasons at Watford in the mid-2000s, including the promotion campaign. Which club did he belong to at the time?
hint: He had moved to Old Trafford from Stoke City in 2005, and years later returned to Watford permanently.

q: Which Watford defender scored the opening goal in the 2006 Championship play-off final against Leeds United?
hint: The American centre-back had been playing non-league football in England only a few years before, and was named man of the match.

q: In which year did the Pozzo family buy Watford?
hint: The takeover was completed in June, a few weeks after that season's Championship campaign ended.

q: Which Italian club did the Pozzo family already own when they bought Watford?
hint: The club from Friuli supplied Watford with a wave of loan signings in 2012-13, including Matěj Vydra and Almen Abdi.

q: Who was the first head coach appointed by Watford after the Pozzo family takeover in 2012?
hint: The former Chelsea and Italy forward took them all the way to the 2013 play-off final in his first season.

q: Who scored the stoppage-time goal that sent Watford to the 2013 play-off final, seconds after Leicester had a penalty saved at the other end?
hint: The striker who finished the counter-attack went on to captain the club to promotion two years later.

q: Which goalkeeper saved Anthony Knockaert's stoppage-time penalty in Watford's 2013 Championship play-off semi-final against Leicester?
hint: The Spaniard, a former Premier League number one, had to keep the ball out twice in the same passage of play.

q: Who was Watford's head coach when they won promotion to the Premier League in April 2015?
hint: The Serb was the last of several men in the dugout that season, taking over in early October.

q: Which club did Watford beat 2-1 away in the 2016 FA Cup quarter-finals?
hint: Odion Ighalo and Adlène Guédioura scored at the Emirates Stadium to knock out the holders.

q: Which club beat Watford 6-0 in the 2019 FA Cup final at Wembley?
hint: The scoreline equalled the record margin of victory in an FA Cup final, first set back in 1903.

q: How many Premier League goals did Odion Ighalo score for Watford in the 2015-16 season?
hint: He was comfortably the club's top scorer that season, finishing with 17 across all competitions.

q: Watford came from two goals down to win the 2019 FA Cup semi-final 3-2 after extra time. Who were their opponents?
hint: Gerard Deulofeu scored twice and a 94th-minute penalty forced extra time.
